newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing - M3 satisfactory but unlikely to reach goal.
newsitem.headline: Issing - M3 satisfactory but unlikely to reach goal.

text.p: Bundesbank directorate member Otmar Issing said on Thursday German M3 money supply growth would probably not slow down enough to reach the four- to seven-percent target corridor this year.
But he added that M3 growth was nevertheless satisfactory.
He also said the trend towards an M3 slowdown remained intact despite the slight increase in annualised growth to 8.7 percent in August from 8.6 percent in July.
"The development of the money supply has returned to a satisfactory course," Issing said, according to the text of a speech.
"We will scarcely be able to reach our goal under which M3 money supply should grow by four percent to seven percent from the fourth quarter of 1995 to the fourth quarter of 1996," Issing said.
"But after the strong expansion in the first quarter of this year, money supply growth slowed down markedly in the second and approached the upper level of the target corridor.
"The recent slight acceleration in August does not fundamentally change this overall pleasing trend," he said.
The Bundesbank usually releases M3 data around the 20th of the month, so September data are expected to be released either at the end of this week or early next week.
The Bundesbank made the text of the speech available in Frankfurt before Issing, who is also the Bundesbank's chief economist, was due to hold at a monetary conference in Luxembourg.
Issing said there were good reasons to be relaxed about the current M3 expansion.

He blamed the growth on reluctance by domestic non-banks to shift funds from deposits included in M3 into longer-term investments, which are not in M3. That process is known as money capital formation.
Issing said money capital formation was kept weak as a result of low interest rates, occasional uncertainty about interest rate movements and the debate about European monetary union.

"Recently calls for a "political interpretation" -- the euphemism for a softening -- of the fiscal convergence criteria are likely to have further unsettled investors in their concern for the value of thier savings," Issing said.
"As a result, funds available long-term are initially being invested on a short-term basis."
